words.en: O you whose shape is the form of Kaumārī
words.g: f. voc. sg. of कौमारीरूपसंस्थाना; compound (see Samāsa)
f. voc. sg. of नारायणी
n. nom. sg. of नमस्; subject of अस्तु
√अस् (adādi, 2P), loṭ (imperative), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
second-person pronoun युष्मद्, dat. sg. (enclitic)

sandhi.note: -e + a- → -e’-: the initial a of अनघे is elided (avagraha).
The m of the prefix सम् becomes anusvāra before s.

samasa.vigraha: मयूराः च कुक्कुटाः च मयूरकुक्कुटाः; तैः वृता मयूरकुक्कुटवृता, तत्सम्बुद्धौ
samasa.type: tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa containing an itaretara dvandva
samasa.sense: attended by the birds of Skanda: the peacock his mount, the cock his banner

samasa.vigraha: महती चासौ शक्तिः च महाशक्तिः; तां धरति इति महाशक्तिधरा, तत्सम्बुद्धौ
samasa.sense: you who hold the great spear (शक्ति), Skanda’s weapon
samasa.alt: शक्ति means both ‘spear’ and ‘power’; ‘bearer of great power’ is possible, but Kaumārī’s weapon in the battle is the śakti-spear (8.17, शक्तिहस्ता), which fixes the first sense. The pun is natural in a hymn to the Śakti.

samasa.vigraha: न विद्यते अघं यस्याः सा अनघा, तत्सम्बुद्धौ
samasa.literal: she in whom there is no sin

samasa.vigraha: कौमार्याः रूपम् कौमारीरूपम्; कौमारीरूपं संस्थानं यस्याः सा कौमारीरूपसंस्थाना, तत्सम्बुद्धौ
samasa.literal: she whose configuration is the form of Kaumārī
samasa.sense: you who appear as Kaumārī, the Śakti of Kumāra (Skanda)
samasa.alt: संस्थान can also be ‘abiding’: ‘she whose abiding is in Kaumārī’s form’ (कौमारीरूपे संस्थानं यस्याः). The sense is the same.

morph.note: वृत is the past participle of √वृ (svādi, ‘to cover, surround’): ‘surrounded, attended’; feminine -वृता, vocative -वृते.
कौमारी is a taddhita from कुमार (with vṛddhi and feminine -ī): ‘belonging to Kumāra’, i.e. Skanda’s Śakti.

mantras.anvaya: (हे) मयूरकुक्कुटवृते महाशक्तिधरे अनघे कौमारीरूपसंस्थाने नारायणि, ते नमः अस्तु।
mantras.anvaya_en: Four vocative epithets of Kaumārī, then the refrain.
mantras.lit: O you who are attended by peacocks and cocks, bearer of the great spear, O sinless one, you whose shape is the form of Kaumārī, O Nārāyaṇī, homage be to you.
mantras.tr: Attended by peacock and cock, holding the mighty spear, spotless one in the form of Kaumārī: O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you.

comm.t: The third Mātṛkā: Kaumārī, the Śakti of Kumāra (Skanda), with his birds, the peacock and the cock, and his great spear.

In the battle Kaumārī came spear in hand, riding a fine peacock, in the form of Guha (8.17), and slew asuras with her spear (8.34, 8.49; 9.38). The peacock is Skanda’s mount and the cock his banner in Purāṇic iconography.
A modern reading: अनघा, ‘sinless’, stands in the middle of a warrior’s description. The force that fights here is pictured as clean of malice.

words.en: O you who have taken up the supreme weapons — conch, discus, mace and the Śārṅga bow
words.g: f. voc. sg. of -परमायुधा; compound (see Samāsa)
प्र + √सद् (bhvādi, 1P, present stem सीद-), loṭ (imperative), madhyama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada

words.en: O you who are in the form of Vaiṣṇavī
words.g: f. voc. sg. of वैष्णवीरूपा; compound (see Samāsa)
f. voc. sg. of नारायणी
n. nom. sg. of नमस्; subject of अस्तु
√अस् (adādi, 2P), loṭ (imperative), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
second-person pronoun युष्मद्, dat. sg. (enclitic)

samasa.vigraha: शङ्खः च चक्रं च गदा च शार्ङ्गं च शङ्खचक्रगदाशार्ङ्गाणि; परमाणि आयुधानि परमायुधानि; शङ्खचक्रगदाशार्ङ्गाणि (एव) परमायुधानि गृहीतानि यया सा, तत्सम्बुद्धौ
samasa.type: bahuvrīhi containing an itaretara dvandva (शङ्खचक्रगदाशार्ङ्ग) and a karmadhāraya (परमायुध)
samasa.literal: she by whom the supreme weapons, conch, discus, mace and Śārṅga, have been taken up
samasa.alt: The participle गृहीत stands between the two groups. The compound may also be divided as शङ्खचक्रगदाशार्ङ्गगृहीता (‘who has taken conch … Śārṅga’, with the participle placed second, as is allowed in such bahuvrīhis) and परमायुधा (‘whose weapons are supreme’); the sense is the same.

samasa.vigraha: वैष्णव्याः रूपं यस्याः सा वैष्णवीरूपा, तत्सम्बुद्धौ
samasa.literal: she whose form is (that of) Vaiṣṇavī
samasa.sense: you who appear as Vaiṣṇavī, Viṣṇu’s Śakti

morph.note: गृहीत is the past participle of √ग्रह् (kryādi, ‘to seize’): the ra of the root becomes ṛ (samprasāraṇa) and the connecting vowel is long (गृह् + ई + त). शार्ङ्ग, Viṣṇu’s bow, is a taddhita from शृङ्ग ‘horn’: ‘made of horn’.
As in 11.3: the only imperative in the refrain verses so far besides अस्तु, a direct prayer inside the salutation.

mantras.anvaya: (हे) शङ्खचक्रगदाशार्ङ्गगृहीतपरमायुधे वैष्णवीरूपे नारायणि, प्रसीद; ते नमः अस्तु।
mantras.anvaya_en: A compound vocative fills the first line; the second adds a prayer (प्रसीद) to the refrain.
mantras.lit: O you who have taken up the supreme weapons — conch, discus, mace and Śārṅga — be gracious, O you in the form of Vaiṣṇavī, O Nārāyaṇī; homage be to you.
mantras.tr: Holding the conch, the discus, the mace and the bow Śārṅga, those supreme weapons, in the form of Vaiṣṇavī — be gracious, O Nārāyaṇī; salutation to you.

comm.t: The fourth Mātṛkā: Vaiṣṇavī, the Śakti of Viṣṇu, holding his four weapons — conch, discus, mace and the bow Śārṅga. In this verse alone of the Mātṛkā series the gods add a prayer, प्रसीद, ‘be gracious’.

In the battle Vaiṣṇavī came seated on Garuḍa, with conch, discus, mace, Śārṅga bow and sword in her hands (8.18), and her discus struck and pierced Raktabīja (8.47–48). Here the name of the refrain and the name of the form coincide: Nārāyaṇī is greeted as Vaiṣṇavī, the power of Nārāyaṇa himself (compare 11.5, वैष्णवी शक्तिः).
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has the names वैष्णवी (892) and विष्णुरूपिणी (893). The two texts are separate works.

sandhi.type: vowel sandhi inside a compound (guṇa); h after a stop
sandhi.note: ā + u → o. Inside उद्धृत (उद् + हृत) the h after d becomes dh.
वसुंधरा takes the augment m after वसु (वसुम्-धरा); the m is written as anusvāra before dh.

samasa.vigraha: उग्रं च तत् महाचक्रं च उग्रमहाचक्रम्; गृहीतम् उग्रमहाचक्रं यया सा गृहीतोग्रमहाचक्रा, तत्सम्बुद्धौ
samasa.type: bahuvrīhi containing a karmadhāraya (उग्रमहाचक्र, itself containing the karmadhāraya महाचक्र)
samasa.literal: she by whom the fierce great discus has been taken up
samasa.sense: you who wield the terrible great discus

samasa.vigraha: दंष्ट्रया उद्धृता वसुंधरा यया सा दंष्ट्रोद्धृतवसुंधरा, तत्सम्बुद्धौ
samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (containing a tṛtīyā relation: दंष्ट्रया उद्धृता)
samasa.literal: she by whom the earth was raised with a tusk
samasa.sense: you who, as the Boar, lifted the earth from the waters on your tusk

samasa.type: upapada tatpuruṣa (with the augment m on the first member)

samasa.vigraha: वराहस्य रूपम् वराहरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति वराहरूपिणी
samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (वराहरूप) with the possessive suffix -in
samasa.literal: she who has the boar’s form
samasa.sense: Vārāhī, the Śakti of the Boar

morph.note: उद्धृत is the past participle of उद् + √हृ ‘to lift up’ (उद् + हृत, with the h aspirating the d: उद्धृत).
रूपिन् ‘having the form of’ (रूप + -in, possessive), feminine रूपिणी, vocative -रूपिणि.

mantras.anvaya: (हे) गृहीतोग्रमहाचक्रे दंष्ट्रोद्धृतवसुंधरे वराहरूपिणि शिवे नारायणि, ते नमः अस्तु।
mantras.anvaya_en: Four vocatives of Vārāhī, then the refrain.
mantras.lit: O you who have taken up the fierce great discus, who raised the earth with your tusk, O you who have the form of a boar, O auspicious one, O Nārāyaṇī, homage be to you.
mantras.tr: Wielding the fierce great discus, raising the earth upon your tusk, auspicious one in the form of the Boar: O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you.

comm.t: The fifth Mātṛkā: Vārāhī, the Śakti of the Boar. She is greeted with the Boar’s great deed: lifting the earth on its tusk.

In the battle the Śakti of Hari, who bears the form of the sacrificial Boar, came in a boar’s body (8.19) and fought beside the others (8.49; 9.39, where her snout crushes asuras). The hymn gives her the Boar’s own deed, the raising of the earth from the waters, so that the deed of Viṣṇu’s avatāra is praised as hers.

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) also knows Vārāhī as a warrior power: name 76, विशुक्रप्राणहरणवाराहीवीर्यनन्दिता, ‘delighted by the valour of Vārāhī, who took Viśukra’s life’. The battles are different and the two texts are separate works.

sandhi.note: Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra.

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (नृसिंह is itself a karmadhāraya: ना एव सिंहः, or नृषु सिंहः — ‘the man who is a lion’)
samasa.literal: by the form of the Man-Lion
samasa.sense: as Nārasiṃhī, the Śakti of Viṣṇu’s Man-Lion

samasa.vigraha: कृतः उद्यमः यया सा कृतोद्यमा, तत्सम्बुद्धौ
samasa.literal: she by whom effort has been made
samasa.sense: you who have set yourself to the task

samasa.vigraha: त्रैलोक्यस्य त्राणम् त्रैलोक्यत्राणम्; तेन सहिता त्रैलोक्यत्राणसहिता, तत्सम्बुद्धौ
samasa.type: tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa
samasa.literal: joined with the protection of the three worlds
samasa.sense: you who are wholly engaged in saving the three worlds

morph.note: Infinitive of purpose (√हन् + tum): ‘in order to slay’, depending on कृतोद्यमे.
त्रैलोक्य is a taddhita (with vṛddhi) from त्रिलोक ‘the three worlds’: ‘the triad of worlds’. सहित ‘accompanied by, joined with’ (सह + हित) here means ‘devoted to’.

mantras.anvaya: (हे) उग्रेण नृसिंहरूपेण दैत्यान् हन्तुं कृतोद्यमे, त्रैलोक्यत्राणसहिते नारायणि, ते नमः अस्तु।
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line is one vocative phrase built on कृतोद्यमे, with an instrumental of manner and an infinitive of purpose; the second adds a further vocative and the refrain.
mantras.lit: O you who, in the fierce form of the Man-Lion, set out with resolve to slay the Daityas, O you who are bent on protecting the three worlds, O Nārāyaṇī, homage be to you.
mantras.tr: In the terrible form of the Man-Lion you rose to slay the demons, intent on saving the three worlds: O Nārāyaṇī, salutation to you.
mantras.tr_note: The vocatives are turned into statements.

comm.t: The sixth Mātṛkā: Nārasiṃhī, the Śakti of the Man-Lion, in her fierce form, set on destroying the Daityas to protect the three worlds.

In the battle Nārasiṃhī came in a body like Nṛsiṃha’s, scattering the stars with the toss of her mane (8.20), and roamed the field tearing asuras with her claws (8.37). As in 11.17, the purpose of Viṣṇu’s avatāra — to protect the worlds from the Daityas — is praised as the Goddess’s own.

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has a related idea in name 80, कराङ्गुलिनखोत्पन्ननारायणदशाकृतिः, ‘from whose fingernails arose the ten forms of Nārāyaṇa’: there too Viṣṇu’s avatāras, the Boar and the Man-Lion among them, come from the Goddess. The two texts are separate works.
